narrativeReportMd:
# SpecimenDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`SpecimenDefinition` keeps its artifact identity, but local R6 changes introduce hard breaks. The highest-impact issues are the new mandatory modifier `status`, `identifier` changing from singleton to repeating, and the additive reference target changing from `Substance` to `SubstanceDefinition`.

## Scope
This report covers local SpecimenDefinition StructureDefinition changes and directly bound terminology. Inherited base-resource and base-datatype differences are excluded.

## Main migration themes
R6 expands SpecimenDefinition into a more canonical definitional artifact, adds R6-only metadata and specimen-use qualifiers, changes one populated JSON shape, and shifts one local reference target to a definitional substance model.

## Highest-impact findings
R4 instances need an R6 `status`; populated R4 `identifier` objects must become arrays; additive references to `Substance` need mapping to `SubstanceDefinition` or to the coded additive branch.

## Findings requiring human review
Human policy is needed for default status assignment, Substance-to-SubstanceDefinition mapping, R6-only workflow qualifier downgrade, and SNOMED container-type expansion impact.

## Follow-up analysis
Review base artifact reports for inherited constraint and datatype issues, and perform terminology expansion review for `specimen-container-type`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `SpecimenDefinition` has material local breaks: R6 requires `status`, changes `identifier` from 0..1 to 0..*, and changes additive references from `Substance` to `SubstanceDefinition`. R6 also adds metadata and workflow qualifiers that are lossy when downgraded to R4.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration must fix required data, serialization shape, and reference targets. R4-to-R6 transforms should assign `status`, wrap `identifier` in an array when present, and map additive references. R6-to-R4 transforms need extension or sidecar policies for new metadata, subject, single-use, and testing-destination content.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural changes because they are directly visible in the R4 and R6 StructureDefinition differentials and snapshots. Confidence is medium for terminology impact because ValueSet compose definitions were compared without live SNOMED CT expansions or official change rationale.

findings.title: R6 adds mandatory modifier status to SpecimenDefinition

newState.summary: `status` is required 1..1 code, summary, modifier, and required-bound to publication-status.

binding.description: Codes identifying the status of a SpecimenDefinition resource.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance can be valid without `status`; R6 requires it. The modifier flag means processors cannot safely ignore it. R6 `status` has no native R4 slot, so downgrade is lossy without an extension or sidecar.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Publication status affects whether a definition should be used operationally.

justification.inferredGoal: Align SpecimenDefinition with governed definitional artifact lifecycle metadata.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `status` optional in the base resource and require it only in profiles or best-practice rules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal is reasonable: R6 treats SpecimenDefinition more like a governed definitional artifact, and a lifecycle `status` is important enough to be a modifier. However, making a new modifier mandatory means every R4 instance without lifecycle metadata is invalid until a status policy is chosen. The less-breaking option is real but only partial because optional status would not guarantee all base R6 definitions expose their usable, retired, or unknown state to generic clients.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would add `status` as `0..1`, possibly with a best-practice warning or conformance profiles requiring it for published catalogs. That would preserve R4-valid instances while giving R6 a native lifecycle field. The tradeoff is material: generic R6 tooling could not rely on every SpecimenDefinition having a modifier status, and status-dependent safety or publication decisions would remain profile- or workflow-specific.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances but weakens uniform lifecycle computability and modifier-aware processing in base R6.

evidence.detail: R4 differential has no `SpecimenDefinition.status` element.
R6 adds `status` with min 1, max 1, type code, isModifier true, isSummary true, and required publication-status binding.
The local CodeSystem includes draft, active, retired, and unknown.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example uses `unknown` only as an illustrative fallback. Real migrations should derive `draft`, `active`, or `retired` when governance data exists.

findings.narrativeMd: `status` is a new required local element. Existing R4 SpecimenDefinition instances often have no publication lifecycle field, so they can fail R6 validation even if all old fields otherwise map.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid occurs whenever an R4 instance lacks `status`. R6-to-R4 is not lossless because R4 has no native `status` element. Strict parsers and generated R6 models will require one of the publication-status codes.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Add an explicit status-assignment rule. Prefer source lifecycle metadata; otherwise document a policy for `unknown` or operationally confirmed `active`. Test missing, valid, and invalid status values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change supports consistent lifecycle governance, but optional base cardinality or profile-level requiredness would have been less disruptive.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for default status policy.

findings.title: identifier changed from singleton to repeating

facts.note: FHIR JSON serializes repeating elements as arrays.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The abstract model was widened, but populated JSON changes shape from an object to an array. R6 instances with multiple identifiers cannot be represented in native R4 without choosing one or using extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Identifier loss or mis-parsing can affect matching, lookup, and catalog governance.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow multiple business identifiers for a specimen definition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `identifier` as `0..1` and add a separate repeating base element for additional identifiers.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple identifiers for a definitional catalog artifact is a reasonable R6 goal. The direct cardinality widening is still disruptive because populated R4 JSON changes from an object to an array. A less-breaking base design exists, but it is only partial because it would split one business concept across two same-resource locations and require clients, searches, and mappings to reconcile them.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would preserve the old singleton `identifier` and add a new repeating element for alternate or additional identifiers. This would keep most R4 instances valid without reshaping JSON. The cost is significant: implementations would need rules for which identifier belongs in the legacy field, searches could miss identifiers unless they aggregate both fields, and the duplicate representation might persist indefinitely rather than converging on one clean R6 model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the JSON shape break but creates duplicate identifier locations, search ambiguity, and a primary/additional distinction that may not be stable.

evidence.detail: R4 cardinality is 0..1.
R6 cardinality is 0..*.

examples.examplesMd: The old example focuses on the singleton identifier shape. It also needs the separate R6 `status` migration to be fully valid in R6.

findings.narrativeMd: `identifier` widened from 0..1 to 0..*. Existing R4 JSON with a populated identifier must be rewritten because R6 expects an array for a repeating element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 JSON instance with `identifier: { ... }` can fail strict R6 parsing because the R6 property is repeating. R6 content with two identifiers is not natively representable in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap existing R4 identifier objects in one-element arrays for R6. For downgrade, define a priority rule for the retained R4 identifier and preserve extras through extensions or sidecar data if needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening is useful but not JSON-wire-compatible. An extension for additional identifiers would have been less disruptive but less clean for R6 tooling.

findings.title: Container additive Reference target changed from Substance to SubstanceDefinition

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path and element id are unchanged; only the Reference targetProfile changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `additiveReference` values pointing to `Substance/...` no longer satisfy the R6 target profile. R6 `SubstanceDefinition/...` references likewise do not satisfy R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Container additives such as preservatives and anticoagulants can be clinically relevant.

justification.inferredGoal: Use the definitional substance model for additives in a definitional specimen resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Allow both `Reference(Substance)` and `Reference(SubstanceDefinition)` target profiles in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using `SubstanceDefinition` is semantically coherent for a definitional specimen resource, but replacing the R4 `Substance` target creates a hard validation break for existing additive references. The same base R6 goal could largely be met by adding the definitional target without removing the old one, so the hard break appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: FHIR `Reference` elements can support multiple target profiles. R6 could have allowed both `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition`, while documentation, examples, or profiles encouraged new definitional references. That preserves most R4-valid instances and still gives R6 a native path to the definitional model. The tradeoff is that R6 clients must handle two substance representations and migration pressure is weaker, but this is a moderate interoperability cost rather than a reason the less-breaking base design would fail.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 references with moderate model-handling cost because clients must support both substance models during transition.

evidence.detail: R4 Reference targetProfile is Substance.
R6 Reference targetProfile is SubstanceDefinition.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments focus on the changed choice element; referenced resources must also exist and conform in a complete instance.

findings.narrativeMd: The additive choice element keeps its name but changes the allowed referenced resource. Implementations using `Substance` resources for additives need a deliberate migration to `SubstanceDefinition` or to the coded branch.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is a target-profile validation break for the Reference branch. The CodeableConcept branch remains structurally valid in both versions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory additiveReference usage. Create or identify corresponding R6 SubstanceDefinition resources, update references, or migrate to additiveCodeableConcept when a code is sufficient. Test both choice branches.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The target replacement is probably semantically justified but avoidable as a hard break by allowing both targetProfiles for a transition period.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed because R4 Substance instances may not map one-to-one to R6 SubstanceDefinition resources.

findings.title: R6 adds optional canonical and publication metadata not native to R4

oldState.summary: R4 lacked native canonical and publication metadata fields on SpecimenDefinition beyond `identifier`.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional url, version, versionAlgorithm[x], name, title, derivedFrom*, experimental, date, publisher, contact, description, useContext, jurisdiction, purpose, copyright, copyrightLabel, approvalDate, lastReviewDate, and effectivePeriod.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The fields are optional, so absence does not break old R4 instances. R6 instances that use them cannot be copied into R4 natively and lose governance metadata if the fields are dropped.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is mainly publication, provenance, and governance loss.

justification.inferredGoal: Make SpecimenDefinition carry canonical-resource style metadata for publication and discovery.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: these are optional R6-only additions that do not make R4 instances invalid in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of adding canonical and publication metadata to SpecimenDefinition is reasonable and aligns the resource with other governed definitional artifacts. Because the added elements are optional, R4 instances are preserved by absence; the compatibility concern is loss when converting richer R6 content back to native R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is applicable for R4-to-R6 base validation because the R6 design does not invalidate old instances. Using R4 extensions, sidecar metadata, or cross-version mappings can mitigate downgrade loss, but those are R6-to-R4 preservation strategies and should not be counted as less-breaking base R6 alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 downgrade may need extensions or sidecars, but that is a preservation mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R4 differential lacks the listed canonical/publication metadata elements.
R6 differential adds the listed optional metadata elements.

examples.examplesMd: Native R4 SpecimenDefinition cannot carry these fields without extensions or external metadata.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 substantially expands the definitional metadata surface. This is not an old-valid/new-invalid issue when absent, but it is a major R6-to-R4 conversion concern.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 validators reject these as unknown native elements if copied directly. Dropping them loses canonical identity, versioning, publisher, jurisdiction, review, or effective-period semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For upgrade, populate metadata from catalog or IG sources where available. For downgrade, define extensions or sidecar persistence for fields that must survive.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Native elements improve R6 consistency and tooling. Extensions would have been more backward-compatible but less discoverable.

findings.title: R6 adds specimen applicability and testing-use qualifiers not present in R4

impact.impactRationaleMd: The fields are optional and do not invalidate old R4 data by absence, but R6 content using them loses applicability or workflow semantics when downgraded to native R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `singleUse` and testing destination can affect specimen routing and reuse decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Capture additional collection applicability and testing workflow semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the subject, single-use, and testing-destination qualifiers are optional additions that preserve R4 instances by absence.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added qualifiers capture plausible applicability and workflow semantics that R4 could not express natively. The exact operational need is not fully explained by the local inputs, so the verdict remains probably rather than definitively justified. Since the elements are optional, however, they do not create an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 alternative is applicable for preserving R4 instances because absence of these optional elements already preserves them. Cross-version extensions or sidecar rules may be necessary when downgrading R6 content to R4, especially for `singleUse` or testing-destination semantics, but those are mitigation strategies rather than alternate base R6 designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Downgrade to R4 may require extensions or external rules; that loss is not a base R4-to-R6 breaking-design issue.

evidence.detail: R4 differential lacks `subject[x]`, `typeTested.singleUse`, and `typeTested.testingDestination`.
R6 adds `subject[x]` as CodeableConcept or Reference(Group).
R6 adds `singleUse` as boolean.
R6 adds repeating `testingDestination` CodeableConcept.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can preserve these semantics only through extensions or external rules.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional but workflow-relevant qualifiers for intended subject, single-use behavior, and testing destination.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is not broken by absence. R6-to-R4 is lossy because direct copying creates unknown elements and dropping them may change routing or reuse behavior.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For downgrade, preserve these fields through agreed extensions or sidecar mappings when they affect operations. For upgrade, derive them only from explicit source catalog data.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Native R6 elements are reasonable, but cross-version extensions would have preserved semantics more easily across R4 and R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is recommended for operational catalogs where single-use or testing destination affects workflow.

findings.title: Several free-text fields changed from string to markdown

newState.summary: The same four fields are markdown.

impact.impactRationaleMd: JSON values remain strings and typical R4 plain text remains valid markdown. The risk is generated primitive type changes and rendering or sanitization behavior for markdown content.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Formatting can affect readability of handling instructions, but the text usually remains carryable.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer formatting for descriptions, requirements, and instructions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the fields typed as `string` and state that markdown syntax may be used.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The local primitive definitions show markdown remains string-valued, so ordinary R4 text is not a direct validation casualty. The break is mostly generated-model, rendering, and sanitization behavior. Richer formatting for descriptions and instructions is a reasonable goal, and a formal `markdown` type gives generic R6 clients a clear signal that plain `string` comments would not reliably provide.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would leave these elements as `string` and update definitions to permit markdown syntax. That would avoid primitive-type changes for generated code and keep R4 content naturally compatible. It is only a partial alternative because generic clients would have to inspect prose or profiles to know that markdown rendering and sanitization are expected; inconsistent handling of formatted handling instructions could then persist.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves generated models and primitive type continuity but loses a formal markdown signal for generic rendering, sanitization, and tooling.

evidence.locator: differential.element for the four text fields
evidence.detail: R4 types are string.

evidence.locator: differential.element for the four text fields
evidence.detail: R6 types are markdown.
Primitive checks showed markdown is string-valued; no additional local hard value restriction was identified for these fields.

examples.examplesMd: R4 can carry the characters as a string, but native R4 consumers have no type signal that markdown rendering is expected.

findings.narrativeMd: Four local instruction/description fields changed from `string` to `markdown`. This is mostly a runtime, codegen, and rendering concern rather than a direct instance-validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Typical R4 string content should remain lexically valid in R6. R6 markdown content downgraded to R4 may be displayed literally or sanitized differently.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated models and rendering paths. Treat migrated R4 text as plain markdown. When downgrading, decide whether to strip markdown or preserve it as literal text.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The formal markdown type gives R6 renderers a clear signal, but comments could have allowed markdown-like content without changing generated primitive types.

findings.title: Specimen container type example ValueSet changed SNOMED filter root

oldState.summary: Example binding to specimen-container-type whose R4 compose filter used SNOMED `is-a 706041008`.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R4 compose uses SNOMED filter concept 706041008.

newState.summary: The binding remains example strength and same canonical ValueSet, but R6 compose filter uses SNOMED `is-a 434711009`.

binding.description: SCT descendants of 706041008 |Device for body fluid and tissue collection/transfer/processing (physical object)|

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 compose uses SNOMED filter concept 434711009. Expansion impact was not measured.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element binding URL is unchanged, but the referenced ValueSet compose differs between package versions.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because the binding is example strength, base validation should not reject existing codes. Picklists, authoring tools, analytics, or profiles that reuse the ValueSet may see different code membership.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Container type coding can influence instructions, but this base binding is not required.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a more precise SNOMED CT hierarchy for specimen containers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable for base instance compatibility because the binding remains example strength.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The package evidence confirms the SNOMED filter root changed, but without a licensed expansion or ballot rationale the correctness and concrete code impact cannot be assessed. Because the binding is still example strength, base R4 instances should not become invalid in R6 solely because of this ValueSet change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: For downstream authoring tools or profiles that depend on the ValueSet, a compatibility include retaining both the old and new SNOMED hierarchies could reduce disruption if expansion comparison shows commonly used old concepts were removed. That is not a base R4-to-R6 compatibility alternative for this element, and it could also preserve an intentionally overbroad hierarchy.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Picklist and profile impacts need expansion review; retaining both SNOMED filters would be a terminology mitigation, not a necessary base-design alternative.

R6 binding remains example strength to specimen-container-type.
R4 compose uses SNOMED CT filter is-a 706041008.
R6 compose uses SNOMED CT filter is-a 434711009.

examples.examplesMd: No concrete removed-code example is included because the local packages did not include SNOMED CT expansions.

findings.narrativeMd: The `container.type` binding is still example strength, but its ValueSet compose changes SNOMED hierarchy. This is not a base validation break, but it can affect suggested-code workflows and derived profiles.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Base R4-to-R6 validation should not reject codes solely due to this example binding. Systems that expand or enforce the ValueSet more strictly may behave differently.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Compare actual local container type codes against R6 expansions when available. Review any profile that strengthens this binding.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Keeping both old and new hierarchy includes could be more compatible, but may retain an intentionally overbroad code set.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology review with a licensed/current SNOMED CT expansion is needed.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Same canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, abstract flag, derivation, and DomainResource baseDefinition.
No R4 local SpecimenDefinition differential elements were removed; all old local paths still exist in R6.
Aside from `identifier` widening and newly added R6 elements, existing local cardinalities remain stable, including `typeTested.preference` at 1..1.
Aside from the additive reference target and string-to-markdown findings, local type choices remain stable. `minimumVolume[x]` remains Quantity(SimpleQuantity) or string.
No local reference target changes were found beyond additive[x].

The required `typeTested.preference` binding retains the same two codes, `preferred` and `alternate`. Most checked example ValueSet compose definitions were unchanged; `specimen-container-type` is reported separately. SNOMED expansions were not available.

No local SpecimenDefinition-specific invariant was identified as added, removed, or strengthened. Observed `ele-1`, `dom-*`, `ext-1`, XPath, and inherited condition differences are base-artifact issues.
No local fixed, pattern, or defaultValue changes were identified.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were identified beyond primitive datatype definitions handled out of scope.
Existing local elements did not gain a material modifier role; the new `status` modifier is reported as a finding.
Existing local summary flags were materially stable. Many new R6 metadata elements are summary elements and are covered by the metadata finding.
No local slicing changes or new local slices were identified.
The main local serialization break is `identifier` becoming repeating and therefore array-shaped in JSON.
R6-only elements and multiple identifiers create downgrade loss as reported; no additional local removals were found.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: StructureDefinition status changed from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is metadata about the StructureDefinition artifact, not an R4 instance element.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Do not confuse this artifact metadata change with the new mandatory instance element `SpecimenDefinition.status`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Required preference binding version changed but codes stayed stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The local CodeSystem still contains `preferred` and `alternate`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Update versioned canonical references from `|4.0.1` to `|6.0.0-ballot4`; no code remapping was identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 explicitly records false flags on many elements
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 often omitted false-valued `mustSupport` and `isModifier`; R6 often records false explicitly. This does not materially change behavior.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Diff tooling should normalize absent false and explicit false. The true modifier `status` is handled separately.
